[csszyx] src/freeze.tsx: the merge table is not one this engine reads (invalid value: integer `-1`, expected u32 at line 1 column 32), so no sz key was merged with a later one it covers.
  help: install the same csszyx version of every @csszyx package, then rebuild; under Turbopack, delete .csszyx/merge-table.json and run `csszyx next prebuild`.
  note: every class is kept, as before 0.18, so `{ pb: 2, p: 4 }` emits both and the stylesheet order decides.

[csszyx] src/freeze.tsx: the merge table is in format 99, and this engine reads format 1, so no sz key was merged with a later one it covers.
  help: install the same csszyx version of every @csszyx package, then rebuild; under Turbopack, delete .csszyx/merge-table.json and run `csszyx next prebuild`.
  note: every class is kept, as before 0.18, so `{ pb: 2, p: 4 }` emits both and the stylesheet order decides.

[csszyx] src/freeze.tsx: source nesting exceeded 64 levels (found 70) — this usually means accidentally or programmatically over-nested sz/JSX. Flatten the structure. (This guard prevents a parser stack overflow.)

[csszyx] AST budget exceeded in src/freeze.tsx: the IR walk stopped mid-file, so the file was left unchanged and contributes NO classes to the safelist. Raise `build.astBudgetLimit` or split the file.
[csszyx] parse error in src/freeze.tsx: the native engine could not fully scan this file (1 syntax error(s))
Unexpected token
oxc parser panicked before csszyx lowering completed
[csszyx] Rust native transform at src/freeze.tsx:28: unsupported dynamic sz attribute; leaving file unchanged for now.
[csszyx] szs at src/freeze.tsx: szs has no effect on a host element — it maps slot names of a custom component. Attribute left unchanged.

[csszyx] szs at src/freeze.tsx: a slot value could not be read at build time, so no slot classes were compiled. Attribute left unchanged.
  Suggestion: Every slot must be an identifier key with a static object literal (or class string) value. For a value only known at runtime, use dynamic() and pass the resulting class string.

szr fallback at 1:22: identifier `cfg` could not be resolved to a static value.
  Suggestion: Make sure it's a module-level or function-body const with a literal object value. For variant-based styling → szv(). For true runtime values → dynamic().

szv catalog at 1:22: identifier `cfg` could not be resolved to a static value.
  Suggestion: Pass the config inline, or as a module-level const object literal. A computed or spread config cannot be read at build time, so none of its variant classes are safelisted and they generate no CSS.

sz fallback at 1:46: key `hover` holds a value only known at runtime and no sz property claims it, so the runtime lowers it and its classes were never collected.
  Suggestion: If the key is a variant, give it a static sz object literal, or a two-branch c ? { … } : { … }; if it is meant as an sz property, check its spelling. For variant-based styling → szv(). For true runtime values → dynamic().

sz fallback at 2:33: imported binding `s` could not be read at build time.
  Suggestion: Export it as a const with a static object literal — a star re-export or a computed value keeps the runtime path, as does build.importedStaticSz: false. For variant-based styling → szv(). For true runtime values → dynamic().

sz fallback at 1:38: identifier `s` could not be resolved to a static value.
  Suggestion: Make sure it's a module-level or function-body const with a literal object value. For variant-based styling → szv(). For true runtime values → dynamic().

sz fallback at 1:38: expression of type `ObjectExpression` is not statically analyzable.
  Suggestion: Use a literal sz object or a module-level const. For variant-based styling → szv(). For true runtime values → dynamic().
[csszyx] unresolvable sz spread at 1:38: sz={{ ...x }} cannot be resolved at build time and falls back to runtime; it may render no styles in production. Use array form: sz={[x, { ... }]}.

[csszyx] possible style override at src/freeze.tsx: this element spreads props that may contain style, while sz emits an explicit style attribute. Move the spread style to an explicit style prop so csszyx can merge both values.

[csszyx] "alignContent" cannot take a runtime value at src/freeze.tsx:1: Tailwind has no utility for this key that reads a CSS variable, so the class and the variable were dropped instead of styling a different property. Name the values with szv(), or use dynamic() for open-ended data.
[csszyx] "p: 1.3" at src/freeze.tsx:1: 1.3 is not on Tailwind's spacing scale (quarter steps only), so the class generates no CSS. Use a quarter step (1.25, 1.5, 1.75) or a unit value ("1.3rem").

[csszyx] "borderT: 'dashed'" at src/freeze.tsx:1: Tailwind has no per-side border style, so this generated no CSS and the class is dropped. Use borderStyle: 'dashed' for every side, or a number on "borderT" for the width.

[csszyx] "p" is a property, not a variant, but received an object { hover } at src/freeze.tsx:1. This compiles to "p:*" classes that match no Tailwind variant and generate no CSS. Move the nested keys up a level, or for color opacity use { color: '...', op: ... }.
[csszyx] maskLinear: unknown field "zzz" at src/freeze.tsx:1 — nothing is emitted for it. maskLinear takes { angle, from, to, t, r, b, l, x, y }.
[csszyx] "touchAction" was removed and takes a runtime value at src/freeze.tsx:1: write auto, none, manipulation on touch, and the other values on touchPanX, touchPanY, touchPinchZoom.

[csszyx] "contain: size" at src/freeze.tsx:1 comes before "containPaint" in one sz object, so containPaint replaces it and the contain value styles nothing. A spread override ({ ...base, contain: 'size' }) leaves this order; to override, layer it: sz={[base, { contain: 'size' }]}.
[csszyx] "touchAction: pan-y" moved to { touchPanY: 'y' } at src/freeze.tsx:1. Run `csszyx migrate` to rewrite it.

[csszyx] mask: 'linear-45' at src/freeze.tsx:1 — gradient layers moved to "maskLinear". Tailwind composites mask-image from one variable per layer, so each layer is its own key. `mask` now takes a direct mask-image only: none, a url(), or a CSS variable.

[csszyx] "touchPanX" takes a runtime value beside "touch" in one sz object at src/freeze.tsx:1, so the build cannot settle them by the object's order: both classes can ship, and Tailwind's stylesheet order picks the one that applies. Layer them, later wins: sz={[{ touch: … }, { touchPanX: … }]}.

[csszyx] <div> at src/freeze.tsx:1:30: class names and `sz` on more than one side of a spread stay separate attributes, one per side: in React, Preact, Solid and Qwik the last one replaces the others, so `card` will not apply there (Vue JSX merges every class instead).
  help: write them in one `sz` array after `{...r}`, in the order that should win: `sz={['card', r.className, { … }]}`.

[csszyx] <div> at src/freeze.tsx:1:29 carries 2 `sz` attributes; they were merged as sz={[first, …, last]}, later wins per property.
  Suggestion: fold them into one sz array so the order is written down.

[csszyx] "weight: '700'" at src/freeze.tsx:1: Tailwind spells a numeric font weight through --font-weight-*, so "font-700" generates no CSS. Write weight: 700 as a number, which brackets to "font-[700]".
[csszyx] "tabularNums" was replaced at src/freeze.tsx:1. Use { numSpacing: 'tabular' } instead, or run `csszyx migrate`.
[csszyx] "inlineFlex" boolean sugar was removed at src/freeze.tsx:1. Use { display: 'inline-flex' } instead, or run `csszyx migrate`.
[csszyx] "maskFrom" was removed at src/freeze.tsx:1: the from stop moved into its layer — maskLinear / maskRadial / maskConic take { from }.
[csszyx] "slashedZero" was replaced at src/freeze.tsx:1. Use { numSlashedZero: true } instead, or run `csszyx migrate`.
[csszyx] Use the canonical key "bg" instead of "backgroundColor" at src/freeze.tsx:1.
[csszyx] sz received a numeric key "0" at src/freeze.tsx:1. This usually means an array or a spread was passed where an object of sz keys was expected. The value is ignored.

[csszyx] Unknown property "xyzzy" in sz prop at src/freeze.tsx:1. The class is still emitted, so it styles nothing unless Tailwind serves that utility. Check for typos. If the class is intentional, define it with Tailwind's @utility.

[csszyx] "container" at src/freeze.tsx:1 is not a variant, but it holds an object, so it lowers to the class prefix "container:" and Tailwind generates no CSS for it. A "--*" key takes a declaration value; "container" takes true.

[csszyx] "nums: oldstyle" at src/freeze.tsx:1 is not a nums value. The class "oldstyle-nums" it emits belongs to { numFigure: 'oldstyle' }: write that key, so it combines with the other groups instead of resetting them. nums takes one of: normal.

[csszyx] "display: bogus" at src/freeze.tsx:1 is not a display value. The class "bogus" is still emitted and styles nothing, unless a rule of your own happens to match it. display takes one of: block, inline-block, inline, flex, inline-flex, grid, inline-grid, contents, table, inline-table, table-caption, table-cell, table-column, table-column-group, table-footer-group, table-header-group, table-row-group, table-row, flow-root, list-item, none.
[csszyx] "bg: 'red-500/50'" at src/freeze.tsx:1 — string slash opacity is not supported, and nothing is emitted for it. Use object form: { color: 'red-500', op: 50 }.
[csszyx] "bg: { color: 'red-500/50', op: 20 }" at src/freeze.tsx:1 — a colour object takes its opacity in op, not in color. Write { color: 'red-500', op: 20 }.

[csszyx] "sz" takes precedence over the runtime "className" on this element at src/freeze.tsx:1, whatever order the attributes are written. If the className carries overrides from a caller, they are dropped.
  Suggestion: state the order in one sz array — sz={[{ … }, className]} for the caller to win, sz={[className, { … }]} for these styles to win.

sz array element at 1:41: this object literal contains a runtime value, so the whole element is deferred to _szPart at runtime (its classes are still safelisted best-effort).
  Suggestion: use finite literal ternary branches when possible, or move truly runtime values to dynamic().
[csszyx] szRecover at src/freeze.tsx: only string-literal values ("csr" | "dev-only") are supported. Dynamic values disable token emission for this element.
